Rescue breathing should not include chest compressions when there is a definite pulse, and breaths must be delivered through an open airway with an appropriate seal.","confidence":1},{"fieldPath":"response","stableId":"response","label":"Missing essential assessment","severity":"error","finding":"The numbered steps move from checking responsiveness directly to compressions without checking whether the person is breathing normally; an unresponsive person who is breathing normally should not automatically receive CPR.","confidence":0.99},{"fieldPath":"response","stableId":"response","label":"Discourages emergency action","severity":"error","finding":"Telling unsure bystanders to let professionals take over can delay lifesaving compressions; they should call emergency services, follow dispatcher instructions, and perform hands-only CPR when appropriate.","confidence":0.99},{"fieldPath":"response","stableId":"response","label":"Incorrect adult compression depth","severity":"error","finding":"The response applies a one-third chest-depth target to adults; standard adult guidance specifies about 2 inches (5 cm), avoiding depths over 2.4 inches (6 cm).","confidence":0.98}]}
